audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is named on nearly every line of the full layer and its cooldown is never given once, and neither layer states the half of the parry that actually punishes Galio.
audit.why: Riposte is 24s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in this lane by a distance, which is what makes 'bait it first' a real plan rather than a slogan. Riot's text: 'Fiora parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time, then stabs in a direction. This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' So it does not merely block your Justice Punch knock-up or Shield of Durand taunt — blocking them upgrades her counter into a stun. Galio's two win conditions are both immobilising effects, which is the whole matchup.
audit.corrected: 24s written into the tldr, winCon, stage lines, cooldown block, do's and all-in windows; the CC-into-stun upgrade written into the don'ts, tradeBad and the key-interactions slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads EVEN while diffRating is 8.5/10, carryRating 10/10 and report[14] calls it a 'Hard matchup'. The full layer also calls Fiora 'him' and 'his' throughout, and report[2] says 'His early — survive to your spikes' even though the chart gives her both item stages.
audit.why: An 8.5/10 difficulty with the enemy holding four of seven stages including the late game is not EVEN, and the lane is not merely 'her early'.
audit.corrected: diff set to HARD, pronouns fixed in every edited line, chart summary rewritten to the actual split.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why calls Stormsurge/Riftmaker your spike on a stage the chart gives Fiora, phases[4].why ends with the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too', and phases[6].why is the same 'best teamfight button in the game' filler.
audit.why: Her spikes are Riposte at 2, Grand Challenge at 6 (110s at rank 1) and her first duelling item; Lunge is 13s at rank 1 and applies on-hit, so she scales with attack speed.
audit.corrected: Stage lines rebuilt on those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math' without naming the heal, and offers boots as a coin flip.
audit.why: Duelist's Dance heals her on every vital hit and Grand Challenge heals her and nearby allies after four vitals or a takedown — those are the two sources. Lunge 'applies on-hit effects', so attack speed is part of her damage and Plated Steelcaps is the boot.
audit.corrected: Both heal sources named, on-hit scaling noted on the Levels 4-5 stage, boots resolved.

edits.before: This is your stabilizing stretch but it is even, not yours — the whole lane bends around her Riposte. If she catches your Justice Punch knockup or your W-taunt release on it she stuns you and the trade is gone, so bait it first: throw a Q or fake the E-dash, watch the parry burn, then commit the real E-knockup into W-taunt while it's down. edits.before: First item is her sharpest knife — a Riposte read on your engage plus Triforce/Ravenous Hydra out-stats you in any side-lane 1v1, so do not try to solo her on a split: she will vital-shred you with true damage your Shield can't soak. Your job late is the thing she can't do — collapse a teamfight with Hero's Entrance, drop the R knockup-taunt onto her carries, and let your Shield finally pay off soaking the enemy mages' burst. By 2+ items your Q waveclear, ramping Shield, and R map presence stabilize the matchup — concede the sidelane and win the 5v5.
